circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit, located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, spans 5. 281 kilometers and was designed by Hermann Tilke to host the final race of the Formula One season since 2009. It became the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue, following Bahrain and preceding circuits established in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit, located in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, is a street course encircling Albert Park Lake that annually hosts the Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside various supporting racing events. The track holds an FIA Grade 1 classification, confirming its status as a premier international racing venue.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following renovations and a name change to the A1-Ring, the track resumed hosting the Grand Prix in the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital that spans 6. 003 km, ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit hosted its first F1 race as the 2016 European Grand Prix, before becoming the home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix starting in 2017.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix that year and continues to stage the annual race alongside various other motorsport categories including GP2 Series and endurance events. The track, which holds FIA Grade 1 status, features multiple configurations and previously accommodated Australian V8 Supercars competition from 2006 until 2010.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya is a 4. 657 km venue featuring a balanced design with extended straightaways and diverse corner configurations that test multiple driving disciplines. The track holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Spa-Francorchamps is a 7. 004 km Belgian circuit situated near the town of Spa in Wallonia that has served as the home of the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix since 1950. The track has maintained continuous Grand Prix hosting since 1985, with only two years of interruption in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361-kilometer track that serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the venue has attracted various international racing series including sports car championships and North American open-wheel and stock car competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit in China's Jiading District has served as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix, which took place there from 2004 until 2019 before returning in 2024. Beyond its primary Formula One event, the venue also began hosting electric racing competitions in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone in Northamptonshire, this English circuit has been synonymous with the British Grand Prix since hosting the inaugural 1948 edition. The venue gained further significance by staging the first-ever World Championship Formula One race in 1950, though it shared hosting duties with Aintree and Brands Hatch for several decades before becoming the permanent home of Britain's grand prix from 1987 onwards.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Mogyoród, hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held within the Eastern Bloc when it opened in 1986, following a recommendation to Bernie Ecclestone by a Hungarian contact instead of racing in the Soviet Union. Constructed in just eight months starting from late 1985, faster than any other F1 circuit, the 4. 381 km permanent facility was built beside a major highway after plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park were rejected by the government.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km Italian racing venue established in 1922 near Milan, making it the third purpose-built circuit globally and Europe's oldest on the continent. Home to the Italian Grand Prix continuously since 1949 (except during 1980 renovations), the track earns its "Temple of Speed" nickname from its extended straights and fast-flowing corners that characterize high-speed racing.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, Japan, is a 5. 807 km motorsport venue with a 155,000-person capacity. The track hosts premier racing competitions, most notably Formula One's Japanese Grand Prix and the Japanese Super Formula championship.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that winds through Paradise, Nevada, incorporating the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding infrastructure. The track passes by some of the city's most iconic venues and landmarks, such as major casinos and hotels that define the Las Vegas entertainment district.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: This 4. 304 km Mexico City venue honors two tragically deceased drivers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, and has served as the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix host in multiple eras. The circuit returned to the championship calendar in 2015 after a 23-year absence, now operating on its modern layout and running under the Mexico City Grand Prix designation since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary street circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida, spanning 3. 363 miles with 19 corners and a qualifying average speed of approximately 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design, the track was purpose-built to host the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the Formula One calendar in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts of Monaco, encircling the harbor area. Though officially named after Monaco itself, it is popularly known as Monte Carlo since the majority of its layout occupies that specific neighborhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the coastal dunes near Amsterdam, the Zandvoort circuit is a 4. 259-kilometre Dutch racing venue that restored Formula One to the Netherlands beginning in 2021 after a lengthy absence. The track will host the Dutch Grand Prix through 2026, following which its tenure in the championship will conclude.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit sits north of Doha in Qatar and features a 5. 419-kilometer layout with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight, holding FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Brazil, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km racing circuit that opened in 1940 and was later renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who tragically died in an aviation accident. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and features an associated kart facility honoring fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coastline that has served as the venue for the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its debut in 2021, while also hosting international electric racing events from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Marina Bay area, incorporating sections of the Downtown Core and Kallang districts as part of its urban layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Montmeló, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a diverse layout combining extended straights with varied corner configurations, making it a balanced test of all-around performance. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 track that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the venue hosts major motorsport events including MotoGP's Motorcycle Grand Prix of the Americas and the Lone Star Le Mans endurance race, along with various other series such as NASCAR.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British driver currently racing for Williams in Formula One, competing under Thailand's flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has secured two world championships during his 23-season career with 32 race victories. Beyond Formula One, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans victories and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both a Formula One title and a World Sportscar Championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli, an Italian driver competing for Mercedes, has secured six Formula One victories following his entry into the sport in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for the Haas team. He competes at the highest level of international motorsport.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One for the Audi team, bringing his competitive experience to the sport's top category.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Bottas is a Finnish racing driver currently competing in Formula One for Cadillac. The veteran driver has achieved ten Grand Prix victories over his thirteen-season career and twice finished as runner-up in the championship standings, both times while driving for Mercedes.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently racing in Formula One with Alpine, competing at the highest level of motorsport representation for his country.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, holds a reserve role with Haas while competing in endurance racing for Nielsen Racing in the LMP2 category. He made seven Formula One race appearances between 2024 and 2025.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: French driver Pierre Gasly currently races for Alpine in Formula One. He previously achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar, a driver of French and Algerian heritage, races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One under the French flag.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, holding joint honours for the most championship titles in the sport with seven victories. He maintains multiple records including the highest number of race wins, pole positions, and podium appearances throughout his career.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from his long career in the sport. Beyond his primary series commitments, Hülkenberg achieved significant success in endurance racing, notably claiming victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while competing for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand racing driver, currently races for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver for Ferrari, has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine seasons in Formula One. He finished as championship runner-up in 2022 while competing for the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver currently competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship with BMW's WRT team and part-time in NASCAR's Cup Series. He previously raced in Formula One across two separate stints, first from 2014 to 2020 and later returning from 2022 to 2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver competing for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship. Across his eight seasons in the sport, he has secured victories in 12 Grand Prix races.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix victory during his time with Alpine remains his sole Grand Prix triumph to date.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Checo Pérez is a Mexican driver currently racing for Cadillac in Formula One. The veteran competitor finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while with Red Bull and has claimed six race victories throughout his 15-season career in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, where he has secured nine Grand Prix victories during his time in the sport across four championship seasons.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing victories in eight Grand Prix races during his career. Known by the nickname "the Honey Badger", he retired from the sport after competing across multiple teams throughout his tenure in the championship.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell, a British motorsport competitor, has secured seven Grand Prix victories during his eight-year tenure in Formula One, currently driving for Mercedes.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes in Formula One for Williams and has secured four Grand Prix victories during his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant participated in Formula One for two seasons between 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously raced in the IMSA SportsCar Championship's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian driver currently competing in Formula One with the Aston Martin team.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver who has held reserve positions with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls throughout his Formula One involvement spanning 2021 to 2025.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen has secured four consecutive Formula One world championships between 2021 and 2024 while racing for Red Bull Racing. With 71 Grand Prix victories accumulated over his 12-season career, he remains one of the sport's most successful contemporary competitors.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is China's sole Formula One competitor to date, having raced in the sport from 2022 through 2024. He currently holds a reserve driver position with the Cadillac team.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Alpine Racing competes as a French-licensed Formula One team based in Enstone, operating as Renault's works outfit until the manufacturer's 2025 withdrawal from the sport. The team rebranded from Renault F1 Team in 2021 to represent the Alpine sports car marque, securing its sole victory under this identity through Esteban Ocon's 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix triumph.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has competed in Formula One through different organizational structures as a British manufacturer, with its current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco branding.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury marque, stands as Formula One's most enduring and accomplished competitor, participating in every World Championship since the series' inception in 1950. Renowned by the nickname "the Prancing Horse" after their iconic emblem, the team has maintained an uninterrupted presence in the sport for over seven decades while accumulating an unmatched record of success.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American Formula One team in 2014, with the squad entering the championship in 2016. Following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024, Ayao Komatsu took over as team principal.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering firm founded by Peter Sauber in 1970, the company initially built sports cars before transitioning to Formula One machinery as an independent manufacturer. The outfit competed in the sport from 1993 until 2025, becoming the fourth-longest-running constructor by race count, whilst also achieving notable endurance racing success including the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours victory. Audi acquired the team and its operations in 2024 to serve as the foundational structure for its own Formula One programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing competes in Formula One as a British outfit headquartered at its Technology Centre in Woking. The team operates as part of the McLaren Group, which is owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One since 1954 as both a team owner and engine supplier, with the current squad operating from Brackley under a German licence and competing as Mercedes-AMG Petronas. Since 2022, the team has been jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff in equal shares. The Mercedes entry is traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows".

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that entered the championship in 2024 as one of two Red Bull GmbH-owned operations alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the team operates as part of the Austrian conglomerate's dual-squad structure in the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024 as one of two Red Bull-owned squads. Based in Faenza with an additional facility in Milton Keynes, the team operates alongside Red Bull Racing as part of the Austrian conglomerate's motorsport portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing competes in Formula One under an Austrian licence while operating from England, forming part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team motorsport portfolio. Established in 2005 and led by Christian Horner for two decades, the team transitioned to Laurent Mekies as team principal in 2025.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, emerging from Williams's prior failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team name and operates from a substantial facility spanning 60 acres.
